title: A-03c: journal store: candidates, verdicts, blocks
spec:
## Goal

The remaining store methods: candidates, verdicts and blocks. Storage and state rules only; deciding whether a verdict is valid is the engine's job in milestone B.

## Design reference

`docs/design/v3-delta-api-alpha.md` section 5 (`candidates`, `verdicts`, `blocks`). `docs/design/v2-candidate.md` section 4 (blocks survive revisions until withdrawn against a new candidate or overridden by the human).

## Deliverables

In package `internal/journal`, added to the `Store` from A-03b. Every method runs in one transaction. Do not change the migrations or the A-03b methods; if something cannot be done without that, stop and report.

- `CreateCandidate(turnID, content, hash) (candidateID, error)`: stores a caller-provided hash. The engine computes candidate identity in milestone B; this method does not hash.
- `RecordVerdict(attemptID, echoedCandidateHash, parsed, reason, validationStatus) (verdictID, error)`: `parsed` is empty, `approve` or `block`. Stores what it is given; it does not judge validity.
- `OpenBlock(verdictID, blockID, candidateHash, severity, evidence, remedy) error`: state `open`. Rejects if the verdict's parsed value is not `block`.
- `WithdrawBlock(blockID, againstCandidateHash) error`: state `withdrawn`, recording the new candidate hash. Rejects unless the block is `open`, and rejects when `againstCandidateHash` is empty or equals the hash the block was opened against (a block is withdrawn against a named new candidate).
- `OverrideBlock(blockID) error`: state `overridden`. Rejects unless the block is `open`.
- `OpenBlocks(turnID) ([]Block, error)`: blocks in state `open` for the turn, across all its candidates.

## Acceptance

- A block opened against candidate hash H1 is still returned by `OpenBlocks` after a second candidate with hash H2 is created for the same turn.
- `WithdrawBlock` with H2 removes it from `OpenBlocks`; with H1 or an empty hash it errors and the block stays open.
- `OverrideBlock` and `WithdrawBlock` each error on a block that is not `open`.
- `OpenBlock` on a verdict whose parsed value is `approve` errors.
- `RecordVerdict` stores each of the four validation statuses and rejects an unknown one.
- `go vet` and lint clean.

## Out of scope

Verdict parsing or validation. Candidate hashing. Turn state changes as a consequence of a verdict. Any network.

title: A-05: fake adapter with scripted failure modes
spec:
## Goal

An in-process `transport.Adapter` that can be scripted to produce every status and failure the contract names, so the engine (milestone B) and the acceptance tests can run without any network or model.

## Design reference

`docs/design/v3-delta-api-alpha.md` section 1 (contract), section 4 item 9 (the fake adapter drives every negative case) and section 6 (verdict envelope text, for the fixtures). `docs/design/v2-candidate.md` section 10 (deterministic failure tests).

## Deliverables

Package `internal/transport/fake`. Standard library only. Do not change `internal/transport` or `internal/transport/contracttest`; if either is insufficient, stop and report.

1. A script: an ordered list of steps. Each step says what the next `Complete` call returns. Step kinds:
   - reply: text, status, native finish reason, transport status, identity, reported model, optional delay;
   - hang: block until the request deadline passes or `Cancel` is called for that attempt, then return `interrupted` with transport status `timeout` or `cancelled` respectively;
   - echo: reply whose text contains a given string, to exercise the scrub.
   A `Complete` call with the script exhausted returns status `error` and a transport status saying so; it never panics and never repeats a step.
2. A constructor taking the script and options: the identity and reported model used when a step does not set them; the `CapabilityRecord` that `Probe` returns; the secret values the adapter pretends it resolved; whether `Cancel` reports server confirmation as `yes` (default) or `unknown`; whether `Usage` is available.
3. `Complete` consumes one step per call, sets `RawOutput` and `Text` to the step's text after `transport.Scrub` with the configured secrets, copies the request envelope into the result, and records the request. A `Calls()` accessor returns every request received, in order, including the full message array, so tests can assert what the engine sent. Safe for concurrent use.
4. `Cancel`, `Probe` and `Usage` per the options above.
5. A `contracttest.Backend` implementation in this package's test file, arranging each case with a one-step script.
6. Verdict fixture helpers, each returning reply text. The envelope format is fixed by delta section 6; copy it exactly.
   - a well-formed approve, given candidate hash and attempt id;
   - a well-formed block, given candidate hash, attempt id, block id, severity, evidence, remedy and reason;
   - prose containing the word "approve" and no envelope;
   - a well-formed approve echoing a different candidate hash than the one given;
   - an otherwise well-formed envelope whose verdict is `approve-with-changes`;
   - output containing two envelopes;
   - a block whose reason contains a line that is exactly `END VERDICT`, followed by more text and a second `END VERDICT`.
   These make milestone B's negative tests one-liners.

## Acceptance

- `contracttest.Run` passes against the fake backend for every case.
- A test drives a script containing every step kind and asserts the sequence of statuses, then asserts the exhausted-script behaviour.
- Hang plus `Cancel` yields `interrupted` with transport status `cancelled`, promptly. Hang with no cancel yields `interrupted` with `timeout` at the deadline.
- An echo step is scrubbed with `ScrubCount` 1 when the echoed string is a configured secret, and returned unchanged with count 0 when it is not (the fake must not scrub what it did not "resolve", mirroring the real contract).
- `Calls()` returns the exact message array passed to `Complete`.
- Fixture smoke test: for the two well-formed helpers, the text between the first line that is exactly `VERDICT v1` and the first later line that is exactly `END VERDICT` contains each required field name from section 6 once. The real parser is milestone B; this only checks the fixtures are well-formed.
- `go test -race` passes for this package.

## Out of scope

Any HTTP. Any verdict parsing beyond the smoke check. Deliberate-mode fixtures.

title: A-06: OpenAI-compatible adapter: complete, cancel, usage
spec:
## Goal

The one HTTP adapter the alpha ships: Chat Completions, non-streaming, parameterized entirely by an endpoint profile. It must pass the contract harness against an `httptest` server. No vendor-specific code paths.

## Design reference

`docs/design/v3-delta-api-alpha.md` section 2 (dialect subset, operational states) and section 1 (secrets, no redirects, scrub, raw output preserved before parsing). `docs/design/v3-addendum.md` section 3 (do not force optional fields; HTTP success is not semantic completion).

## Deliverables

Package `internal/transport/openai`. Standard library plus this repository's packages. Do not change `internal/transport`, `internal/transport/contracttest` or `internal/config`; if any is insufficient, stop and report.

1. A constructor taking a `config.EndpointProfile` and a `config.SecretResolver`, returning an adapter that implements `transport.Adapter`. `Probe` returns `transport.ErrNotImplemented` until A-07a.
2. `Complete` request:
   - `POST {BaseURL}/chat/completions`. The JSON body has exactly four keys: `model` (from the request), `messages`, `stream` set to false, and the max-tokens key named by the profile's `MaxTokensField` (`max_tokens` when that is empty). No temperature, stop, seed, response_format, tools or any other key.
   - A message whose role is not system, user or assistant makes `Complete` return a Go error without sending anything.
   - The profile's `Auth` and each `ExtraHeaders` value are resolved through the resolver immediately before the request and used only to set headers (`Authorization: Bearer <value>` for `Auth`). A resolver error makes `Complete` return a Go error without sending anything. Resolved values are not stored on the adapter and are not logged; header values are never logged.
   - The HTTP client refuses any redirect whose target host differs from the profile's host, and uses a per-request context bounded by the request deadline.
   - Exactly one HTTP request per `Complete`. No retry, backoff or failover.
3. `Complete` result. `RawOutput` is the full response body as received, scrubbed with the values resolved for this request; `ScrubCount` is the number of substitutions in it. `Text` is the first choice's message content, parsed from the unscrubbed body and then scrubbed separately. The envelope is copied from the request. Mapping:

   | Observation | Status | Transport status |
   |---|---|---|
   | 2xx, parseable, `finish_reason` `stop` | `complete` | `ok` |
   | 2xx, parseable, `finish_reason` `length` | `truncated` | `ok` |
   | 2xx, parseable, `finish_reason` `content_filter` | `refused` | `ok` |
   | 2xx, parseable, any other or missing `finish_reason` | `error` | `ok` |
   | 2xx, body not parseable or no choices | `error` | `malformed_body` |
   | body larger than the limit (option, default 16 MiB) | `error` | `body_too_large` |
   | 401 or 403 | `error` | `unauthorized` |
   | 404 | `error` | `model_unavailable` |
   | any other non-2xx | `error` | `http_<code>` |
   | redirect to another host refused | `error` | `http_<code>` of the redirect |
   | connection refused or DNS failure | `error` | `unreachable` |
   | deadline passed before the body was fully read | `interrupted` | `timeout` |
   | cancelled through `Cancel` | `interrupted` | `cancelled` |
   | connection lost mid-body | `interrupted` | `reset` |

   The native `finish_reason` is preserved verbatim in `NativeFinish` whenever the body carried one. Status is never inferred from the content of the answer.
4. Identity. `ReportedModel` is the response's `model` field verbatim, or empty. `Identity` is always unknown in this task: no field of the Chat Completions response is treated as a digest or revision (see `docs/design/open-questions.md`, OQ-1). Do not derive an identity from the model name.
5. `Cancel(attemptID)`: cancels that attempt's in-flight request. `Requested` is true when an in-flight request was found; `ServerConfirmed` is always `unknown`, because HTTP gives no evidence of server-side termination. Safe to call concurrently with `Complete`.
6. `Usage`: the most recent response's `usage` block if it had one, else `transport.ErrUsageUnavailable`. Each `CompleteResult` also carries its own usage when present.
7. A `contracttest.Backend` implementation in this package's test file, backed by `net/http/httptest`: one handler behaviour per case, a second server as the foreign host for `redirect_other_host`, and for `secret_echo` a handler that puts the received bearer token into the answer content.

## Acceptance

- `contracttest.Run` passes for every case.
- The request body for a default profile has exactly the four keys above; with `MaxTokensField` set to `max_completion_tokens` that key is used instead of `max_tokens`.
- A 302 to a second `httptest` server results in zero requests reaching it.
- `finish_reason` `length` with answer content shaped like an approving verdict envelope is still `truncated`.
- A table test covers each row of the mapping table that the contract harness does not (404, missing `finish_reason`, no choices, oversize body, connection refused, cancel).
- With the standard logger redirected to a buffer for the whole test run, the bearer value never appears in it.
- `go test -race` passes for this package.

## Out of scope

Streaming. Probe (A-07a). Optional request parameters. Any dialect other than Chat Completions. Any real endpoint.
